output.summary: Flowering arum native to rainforests of Maritime Southeast Asia, New Guinea and Australia’s Murray Islands. Its giant heart-shaped leaves can serve as makeshift umbrellas; its starchy rhizome, above-ground stem, leaves and leaf stalks are used as food but must be thoroughly cooked because its irritating sap contains needle-like calcium oxalate crystals.
